text_content:
Level 1: Halo slides
Halo slides are dramatic, punchy, and impactful. They are unapologetically IBM and it shows. A Halo deck should use no more than 20 slides to tell its story.

Keynote
Template guidelines
—
Template slide types

Level 2: Business slides
Business supporting slides. Including business outcome, client stories, demo, the pricing and timeline that reflect from the RFP etc.

Level 3: Technical slides
Deep technical content include Architecture diagrams, chart, etc. Find the components to build these in the Offering Kit building guidelines.

This template is broken into 3 levels to help you use the most appropriate slide to tell the story you are trying to convey.

Level 1 Halo slides are the least text dense and lean on “showing and not telling”, using visual experiences to communicate.

Level 2 and Level 3 slides can't be as visually punchy as a Halo slide, yet using IBM brand and supporting images can look exciting and communicate at a more nuanced level.
—
Guiding Design Principle: This template has been painstakingly researched and intentionally coordinated with brand templates. Everything in this theme works together with approved IBM Brand Master Templates. 

For further template guidance and details you can go to the Offerings Space. For the brand approved template you can find them all on the brand resources page.

text_content:
Step 1: Data Collection - We need to gather lots of information, like pictures, videos, or words, to help our AI learn and understand what our client wants.
Step 2: Data Cleaning - We need to make sure the information we collected is correct and not messy, so our AI can understand it properly.
Step 3: Model Building -  We use the cleaned information to build a special kind of computer program called a model, which will help our AI make decisions or do tasks.
Step 4: Testing and Deployment - We test the model to make sure it works correctly, and then we give it to our client so they can use it to make their life easier.

Speed, Efficiency & Automation, Customer experience, Agent experience.
Quick access to a knowledge base based on which responses to customer’s queries are automatically generated. The agent uses the responses to promptly react during the interaction via any channel.

Conversation Summarization

Speed, Efficiency & Automation, Agent experience
During handover and after contact work, the agent is presented with the interaction summary (structured or unstructured) highlighting the key information needed for quick decision making or providing conversation wrap up notes for further use.

Information Extraction

Speed, Efficiency & Automation

Automated Email Handling

text_content: We have identified a set of recommendations to address concerns around data

Over the past 4 years, the data team put in place a framework for managing and governing data at Hyatt & established an operating model, centered around 19 data pods (e.g., Finance, Forecasting), that includes:

In addition, stood up a technology environment for managing data, which continues to evolve (e.g., Informatica MDM for managing master data, SnowFlake Data Lake to house data in common environment, ThoughtSpot Self-Service [85% of Hyatt legacy data in Hyatt’s lake today], GEM 2.0 to create a robust customer view)
However, more work still needs to be done. There are a number of “wishes” that have been expressed by various data users:
Following is a table of recommendations that addresses these wishes
Data product catalog that describes the products the data team provides

Data stewards from business 
who are responsible for ensuring data in their pod meets business needs and maintaining data

Data product agile POD’s
that are responsible for curating, engineering APIs, and executing against the roadmap

Established governance cadence 
that includes quarterly capacity/roadmap reviews, quarterly release notes, data community events and discussion

“I want a more robust customer view, that incorporates external data sources”
“I want to bring in data quickly so I can begin experimenting, I don’t want to wait for the data management processes to play out”
“I want more transparency, for example, I want a catalog where I can see all data across enterprise. Yes, we have data stewards, but they have a narrow data view”
“I want my data to be consistent across systems, it is frustrating that some measures are different across systems”
“I want to get access to data I need quickly, the process to get access is cumbersome”
“I want clarity on process including timing, the data team can never seem to give me a straight answer on timing/process etc…”
